title: Slap
blurb: Sharp, crisp, and considerably louder than physics permits. Cinema slaps have been unrealistically amplified for decades — foley artists build them from leather, gloves and enthusiastic hand-clapping — because a genuine slap sounds disappointingly soft and the audience refuses to accept it. Editing inherited the whole convention. It works on everything: a reality check landing, a punchline arriving, the exact moment somebody says a thing that deserves consequences. One of the most-used impacts in the business, and we are happily continuing the tradition of overstating it.
